text: Writing clean code is a skill that pays off in the long run. The main goal is to make your code readable, not just for the computer, but for other people—and for your future self. A good starting point is using clear naming conventions. For example, instead of calling a variable `x`, use something like `userAge` so its purpose is obvious. Another key habit is to keep functions short and focused on a single task. A function should do one thing and do it well; if it gets too long, break it into smaller pieces. This approach greatly improves maintainability, making it easier to update, fix, and extend your code without causing new bugs. In short, clean code saves time and reduces frustration.
